id: title:arnohillen:stop scanners inventing findings on irrelevant sessions

review.posthog_relevance: Replay Vision classification and scoring behavior, specifically the generation of reasoning, tags, and scores for session analysis.
review.reason: The chunk supplies prompt templates and instructions for the Replay Vision classification and scoring system. P1.F1.H1 adds instructions to the classifier prompt, P1.F2.H1 adds instructions to the preamble prompt, and P1.F3.H1 adds instructions to the scorer prompt. These changes establish the behavior of the classification and scoring system, including how the model should handle,
review.uncertainty: The chunk does not demonstrate the actual classification and scoring results, so the benefit and effectiveness of these changes cannot be established.

observations.limitations: This chunk only supplies prompt templates and tests; it does not show the runtime execution, scoring, or classification results, so actual behavior and benefit cannot be established.

observations.behavior: Adds a new XML-like block and instruction to the preamble prompt, requiring the model to explicitly state when a session does not reach the criterion and to keep confidence low.
observations.code_quote: The criterion you're given often targets a specific flow, screen, or behavior, and the recording you're watching may never reach it. That is a normal outcome of broad recording filters, not something to explain away: open your `reasoning` by saying the session doesn't show it, and keep `confidence` at or below 0.3. Never stretch an unrelated part of the session to fit the criterion, and never reason about what the user would have done had they gone there.
observations.posthog_connection: This could help reduce false positives and hallucinated findings in the Replay Vision classification and scoring, but the chunk does not demonstrate the scoring or classification results.

observations.behavior: Adds an instruction to the classifier prompt requiring a tag even when the session does not show the criterion, and to use the least wrong option and keep confidence low.
observations.code_quote: In `reasoning`, work through what the session shows that bears on this; then choose tags from this fixed vocabulary: [{{ vocabulary }}]. {% if multi_label %}Pick every tag that applies.{% else %}Pick exactly one tag.{% endif %} A tag is required even when the session never shows what the criterion describes, so in that case pick the least wrong one and follow the relevance rules: lead the `reasoning` with the fact that the session doesn't show it, and keep `confidence` low.
observations.posthog_connection: This could help ensure consistent classification behavior, but the chunk does not demonstrate classification results.

observations.behavior: Adds an instruction to the scorer prompt requiring a score even when the session does not show the criterion, and to stay away from both ends of the scale.
observations.code_quote: In `reasoning`, work through what you observed in the session that bears on this criterion, noting what the events confirmed or contradicted; then set `score` on {% if scale_label %}the '{{ scale_label }}' scale{% else %}the scale{% endif %} from {{ scale_min }} to {{ scale_max }}. A score is required even when the session never shows what the criterion describes, so in that case follow the relevance rules and stay away from both ends of the scale: an extreme score reads as a real finding, and there's nothing here to find.
observations.posthog_connection: This could help prevent extreme scores from being assigned to inapplicable sessions, but the chunk does not demonstrate scoring results.
